test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Govind bought two items at a total cost of ₹4,800. He sold one item at 34% profit and the other at 10% loss. If Govind sold both the items together for ₹5,442, then what is the difference between the cost price (in ₹) of both the items?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total profit in value = 5442 − 4800 = 642.

Total profit % = (642 ÷ 4800) × 100 = 13.375%.

Using **Allegation**: (Profit1: 34%) and (Loss2: −10%) with mean (13.375%).

Ratio of CP = (13.375 − (−10)) : (34 − 13.375) = 23.375 : 20.625 = 187 : 165 = 17 : 15.

Total parts = 17 + 15 = 32. Since 32 parts = 4800, 1 part = 150.

Difference = (17 − 15) × 150 = 2 × 150 = 300.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → Total **Cost Price (CP)** = 4800, Total **Selling Price (SP)** = 5442, Profit1 = 34%, Loss2 = 10%.
Formulas: Profit = SP − CP | CP₁ + CP₂ = Total CP | SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dcd9a458d811d17d608f03cf2dda169c395f399ebfa1256d344f5d3b39119db9.png] 
⇒ Let CP of first item be x and second item be (4800 − x).
⇒ SP₁ + SP₂ = 5442.
⇒ x × (1.34) + (4800 − x) × (0.90) = 5442.
⇒ 1.34x + 4320 − 0.90x = 5442.
⇒ 0.44x = 5442 − 4320 = 1122.
⇒ x = 1122 ÷ 0.44 = 2550.
⇒ CP₁ = 2550, CP₂ = 4800 − 2550 = 2250.
⇒ Difference = 2550 − 2250 = 300.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation Method

When two components are mixed to form a whole, the ratio of the quantities is the inverse of the difference between the components and the mean.

Profit and Loss on CP

Unless otherwise stated, **Profit%** and **Loss%** are always calculated on the **Cost Price**.
